title: Runtime Cost Instrumentation and Alerting Guidelines
author: Maya Singh
content:
Overview

This page defines how the platform teams instrument runtime activity for cost visibility, defines guardrail alerts for cost drift, and prescribes investigation and mitigation runbooks. The goal is to detect anomalous cost events (hourly/daily), tie them back to traffic/model/route changes, and automate low-friction mitigations while preserving customer SLAs.

Why this matters

- Cloud and GPU costs are the largest controllable expenditure for Redwood inference.
- Cost surprises often come from operational shifts (batching, model rollouts, token inflation) that are detectable in telemetry.
- Faster detection + clear remediation reduces MTTX (mean time to mitigate) and preserves budget/finance predictability.

Scope

Applies to: Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private control-plane metrics ingestion for customers using Redwood-managed telemetry. Does NOT change billing contracts or billing export formats — it augments observability for platform/operators.

Key concepts and metrics

- Unit cost (derived): cost_per_token = cloud_costs_allocated / tokens_generated (hourly/day).
- Effective throughput cost: cost_per_request = cloud_costs_allocated / requests_served (useful for short-running low-token calls).
- Model usage breakdown: tokens_per_model, requests_per_model, avg_latency_per_model.
- Batch efficiency: avg_requests_per_batch, tech_latency_overhead_ms.
- KV/cache hit ratio: prefix_cache_hit_rate — impacts effective token compute.

Minimum telemetry to emit (per-service)

Every runtime service must export the following Prometheus-style metrics (or mapped equivalents):

- runtime_tokens_total{model,route,customer_tier} (counter)
- runtime_requests_total{model,route,customer_tier,response_kind} (counter)
- runtime_gpu_seconds{instance_type,pool,region} (histogram/counter)
- runtime_batch_size{model,pool} (histogram: observed batch sizes)
- runtime_kv_cache_hits_total{model,route} and runtime_kv_cache_misses_total{model,route}
- runtime_error_responses_total{code,model,route} (counter)
- runtime_request_latency_ms_bucket{le,model,route} (histogram)

Mapping to cost: a periodic job (cost-allocator) ingests cloud billing (hourly granularity), maps resource costs to pools/instances, and divides cost across runtime metrics to produce derived timeseries: cost_per_gpu_second, cost_per_token, cost_per_request.

Dashboard layout (recommended panels)

1) Cost overview (24h / 7d)
   - Line: total_allocated_cost (USD) by pool
   - Line: cost_per_token (USD) 24h rolling average
   - Bar: top 10 models by spend (last 24h)

2) Efficiency heatmap
   - Matrix: avg_batch_size vs cost_per_token per model
   - Scatter: kv_cache_hit_rate vs cost_per_token

3) Anomaly detector panel
   - Spike detector for cost_per_token and total_allocated_cost (z-score / rolling baseline)

4) Live incident view
   - Top open alerts, correlated traces (link to tracing UI), top slow endpoints

5) Attribution explorer
   - Queryable panel: breakdown by route/model/customer_tier/time_range (supports ad-hoc investigation)

Sample Grafana queries

- Cost per token (PromQL pseudo):
  sum(rate(cloud_cost_allocated_usd_total[1h])) by (pool) / sum(rate(runtime_tokens_total[1h])) by (pool)

- Top models by spend (PromQL pseudo):
  topk(10, sum(rate(cloud_cost_allocated_usd_total[1h])) by (model))

Alerting rules and thresholds

Suggested baseline rules (Alertmanager/CloudWatch equivalents):

1) cost-drift-high: triggers when cost_per_token rises > 30% vs 7-day rolling median for a single model OR total_allocated_cost rises > 25% vs 24h baseline and absolute delta > $2000 within 1h.
   - Severity: P2
   - Pager: oncall-platform -> 15m acknowledgement, escalate to platform-eng lead if not acked in 30m.

Prometheus alert example (yaml snippet):

```yaml
groups:
- name: runtime-cost-alerts
  rules:
  - alert: CostPerTokenSpike
    expr: |
      (
        (sum(rate(cloud_cost_allocated_usd_total[1h])) by (model) / sum(rate(runtime_tokens_total[1h])) by (model))
        / on(model) (avg_over_time((sum(rate(cloud_cost_allocated_usd_total[1h])) by (model) / sum(rate(runtime_tokens_total[1h])) by (model))[7d:1h]))
      ) > 1.3
    for: 15m
    labels:
      severity: page
      area: runtime-cost
    annotations:
      summary: "Model {{ $labels.model }} cost per token >30% above 7d median"
      runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/runtime-cost-instrumentation-and-alerting-2026#investigation-playbook"
```

2) unexplained-spend-surge: total_allocated_cost increase > 50% over previous 2h rolling average AND not explained by known scheduled events (labels: maintenance=true).
   - Severity: P1 if delta > $10k/hr or P2 otherwise.

3) batch-efficiency-degradation: avg_requests_per_batch drops by >40% for a pool while request volume is steady (>95th percentile).
   - Severity: P2. Suggests new consumer behavior or misconfigured client.

Investigation playbook (first 20 minutes)

1) Triage (0-5m)
   - Check alert details and Grafana panel. Note time window and affected model/pool/route.
   - Confirm whether the alert correlates with a deployed change (check CI deploy pipeline / rollout tags).
   - Record initial hypothesis in the incident channel (#platform-cost-alerts).

2) Rapid attribution (5-15m)
   - Run attribution queries: tokens_by_model_1h, requests_by_route_1h, gpu_seconds_by_pool_1h.
   - Query trace service for top slow/expensive requests: `traces?service=runtime&tags=model:<model>`
   - Check customer-facing incidents (CS and support tickets) for correlated activity.

3) Mitigation (15-60m)
   - If cause is client-side (sudden traffic spike): open temporary rate-limit or burst-cap policy for the offending route with a 30m TTL.
   - If cause is model rollout regression (new variant with larger response tokens): Roll back to prior stable model via canary rollback and mark for evaluation.
   - If cause is infrastructure (bad actor, runaway job): cordon pool nodes, scale down poorly behaving autoscaler policy, and spin up replacement nodes in unaffected pool.

4) Communication (parallel)
   - Post interim update within 30m to #platform-status and relevant on-call pager channel.
   - If customer impact suspected, notify Customer Success within 60m.

5) Post-incident (within 48h)
   - Create a short incident summary with root cause, timeline, and action items.
   - Tag the incident with labels: root_cause, mitigation, budget_impact, and link to cost dashboards.

Required playbook commands and snippets

- Rate-limit (example CLI stub):
  ```bash
  rdlctl routes apply --route my-customer-route --policy rate_limit=100/s --ttl 30m
  ```

- Rollback example (canary rollback):
  ```bash
  rdlctl rollout rollback --deployment-id dp-12345 --to-version v2026-02-10
  ```

- Cost attribution query (SQL pseudo against events warehouse):
  ```sql
  SELECT model, sum(tokens) as tokens, sum(gpu_seconds) as gpu_seconds,
         sum(allocated_cost_usd) as cost
  FROM runtime_events_hourly
  WHERE ts >= now() - interval '3 hours'
  GROUP BY model
  ORDER BY cost desc
  LIMIT 50;
  ```

Ownership and escalation

- Primary owners: eng-platform -> runtime-observability subteam (pager handle: @platform-oncall).
- Secondary owners: eng-sre for capacity actions, eng-serving-runtime for model rollouts.
- Finance alerting: when an alert has an estimated hourly delta > $5k, finance-notify must be triggered (automated webhook).

On-call responsibilities

- Acknowledge within 15 minutes.
- Start investigation within 30 minutes.
- Declare P1 and involve rotation lead within 45 minutes.

Guardrails and SLOs (cost hygiene)

- Cost Drift SLO: no model should exceed 25% increase in cost_per_token month-over-month without a documented change request.
- Efficiency SLO: average batch size for production pools should remain >= 75% of observed 90-day median.
- Alert noise target: <3 actionable cost alerts per week across the platform teams.

Retrospective checklist (after actioning)

1) Timeline and root cause written, labeled, and linked to commit/deployment if applicable.
2) Update monitoring queries to reduce false positives (if applicable).
3) Add synthetic checks, e.g., token-per-request sanity checks to catch slow regressions.
4) Add a cost guard to the release checklist for model variants that can increase average token outputs by >10%.

Roadmap (near-term items)

- Q2 2026: Automate attribution playbook: one-click drilldown from alert to prefilled SQL + Grafana URL.
- Q3 2026: Per-customer cost anomaly detection and auto-tagged chargebacks for Dedicated pools.
- Q4 2026: Integrate model-eval metrics (quality regressions) into cost alerts to avoid blind rollbacks.

Appendices

A. Tagging and labeling conventions

- model: <model_name> (e.g., redwood-m1-7b)
- pool: <pool_name> (e.g., hosted-gpu-a100-1)
- route: canonical route id used by ingress
- customer_tier: free | standard | enterprise

B. Example incident summary template (required)

- Title: short descriptor with timeframe
- Impact: estimated spend delta and affected customers
- Timeline: bulletized 5–10 events with timestamps
- Root cause: one-line root cause
- Mitigation: what was done to restore baseline
- Action items: owners and due dates

C. Links and references

- Tracing UI: https://tracing.redwood.internal/
- Cost allocator docs: /confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/cost-allocator-architecture-2025
- Release checklist: /confluence/eng-platform/how-tos/release-checklist-rls

If you have suggestions or want additional panels/alerts added to the org dashboard, open a PR against `infra/observability/dashboards` and tag @platform-observability.
